item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00229","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C01","C03","C04"],"selected_candidate_label":"C01","confidence":0.96,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C01 is a highly plausible drafting source. It was issued only one week earlier, establishes the same United States High Commissioner for Germany, and uses the distinctive supervisory formula later adapted in the child: authority exercised “under the immediate supervision” of a named superior, “subject, however, to consultation with and ultimate direction by the President.” The child reuses that concrete legal-administrative machinery while adding the High Commissioner’s representation of the economic-cooperation officials and the supporting Chief of Special Mission. C03 is relevant to the Administrator for Economic Cooperation and delegated field administration, while C04 mentions the chief of special mission, but neither supplies language or structure as materially close as C01.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"During his tenure of office as United States High Commissioner for Germany, Mr. John J. McCoy, under the immediate supervision of the Administrator for Economic Cooperation and the coordination of the United States Special Representative for Europe subject, however, to consultation with and ultimate direction by the President)","parent_excerpt":"The United States High Commissioner for Germany ... shall have the authority, under the immediate supervision of the Secretary of State (subject, however, to consultation with and ultimate direction by the President)","explanation":"Distinctive supervisory and presidential-direction language is reused for the identical office, with the supervising officials adapted to the child's economic-cooperation function."},{"child_excerpt":"shall be the representative of the said Administrator and the said Special Representative in all their relations and actions with respect to Germany","parent_excerpt":"The High Commissioner shall be the supreme United States authority in Germany ... including the representation of the United States on the Allied High Commission for Germany","explanation":"Both define the High Commissioner’s representative authority in Germany, with the child narrowing that machinery to relations and actions undertaken for economic-cooperation officials."}]}
